A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ControlHair and contain 21 readable pages, including the same equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A-D. All content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original quantitative comparisons in Table 2, generated-video examples, runtime measurements, and dataset and failure analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original quantitative comparisons, generated-video examples, runtime measurements, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The three-stage simulation, control-signal extraction, and conditioned video diffusion pipeline is unchanged, including its components and training procedure (Sec. 4).

E1.justification: Both retain the 10K-video training dataset, FFHQ-Wild images, VEO 2 reconstruction evaluation, three application tasks, and full-body/anime and failure scenarios.

E2.justification: Wan 2.1 and UniAnimate-DiT remain the same evaluated comparators in Figure 5 and Table 2. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The 10-video reconstruction evaluation, 81-by-832-by-480 output dimensions, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, training budget, and simulator settings are unchanged (Sec. 5).

E4.justification: Appendices B-D retain identical dataset-diversity analyses, full-body and extreme-motion examples, and reconstruction-error and correction cases. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both average reconstruction metrics across video frames and report no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All Table 2 scores, runtime measurements, dataset percentages, and qualitative findings are unchanged. ControlHair retains PSNR 17.15, SSIM 0.668, and LPIPS 0.370.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and mathematical definitions in Equations 1-7 are identical. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about physics control, simulator-diffusion integration, easier annotation, comparative performance, and applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations of controllability and error correction remain unchanged, as do limitations involving reconstruction, simulation, kinky hair, large motion, and offline generation.

D1.justification: Simulator defaults, pretrained components, LoRA rank, optimization settings, hardware, runtime descriptions, and project-page access information are identical. Separating the Training paragraph adds no technical information.

R1.justification: The same 58 references and related-work discussions are retained, with unchanged novelty claims and positioning relative to earlier simulation and video-generation methods.

P1.justification: v4 separates Training from the preceding dataset paragraph in Sec. 4.3 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Wording and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The paragraph break reflows text on page 10; word spacing changes in the conclusion's final line on page 15, and the arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: Separating the Training paragraph slightly improves readability, but the remaining edits are typographic or version metadata. The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, leaving overall paper quality materially unchanged.
